# Follow commands: follow, unfollow, followers, following

## `fpt follow`

Make USER follow ENTITY.

USER is a HumanUser (HumanUser:42 or JSON) and ENTITY any entity (Type:123 or JSON). Prints the result, which has "followed": true.

```text
fpt follow [OPTIONS] USER ENTITY
```

Library call: `Shotgun.follow`.

Options:

- `--dry-run`: Print the library call instead of making it.

Examples:

```shell
fpt follow HumanUser:42 Shot:1234
fpt follow HumanUser:42 Shot:1234 --dry-run
```

## `fpt followers`

List the users who follow ENTITY.

ENTITY is any entity, as Type:123 or JSON. Prints a list of HumanUsers with their names and status.

```text
fpt followers [OPTIONS] ENTITY
```

Library call: `Shotgun.followers`.

Examples:

```shell
fpt followers Shot:1234
```

## `fpt following`

List the entities USER follows.

USER is a HumanUser, as HumanUser:42 or JSON. Narrow the list with --project and --entity-type; without them it holds everything the user follows, which can be long.

```text
fpt following [OPTIONS] USER
```

Library call: `Shotgun.following`.

Options:

- `--project Project:ID|JSON`: Only entities in this project.
- `--entity-type TYPE`: Only entities of this type.

Examples:

```shell
fpt following HumanUser:42 --project Project:70 --entity-type Shot
```

## `fpt unfollow`

Make USER stop following ENTITY.

USER is a HumanUser (HumanUser:42 or JSON) and ENTITY any entity (Type:123 or JSON). Prints the result, which has "unfollowed": true.

```text
fpt unfollow [OPTIONS] USER ENTITY
```

Library call: `Shotgun.unfollow`.

Options:

- `--dry-run`: Print the library call instead of making it.

Examples:

```shell
fpt unfollow HumanUser:42 Shot:1234
```
